rationale:
Obligations and their tests:

1. `from_path` returns the root contents for a file, using the supplied cache. `file_constructors_infer_the_language_and_return_addressed_contents` asserts that the root selector is empty, that `text()` equals the whole source, that the fingerprint matches `from_source`, and that the outline items are `["", "fn[check_token]"]`. `domain_clones_share_the_first_successful_outline_for_each_path` covers the cache. A failed first load is not cached. The first successful snapshot is reused by `peer.cache()` even after the file is edited and removed. This is checked with `ptr::eq` on the outline, the original text and an equal fingerprint. A fresh cache sees the new content.

2. `from_id` uses the same cached file and selects the addressed item. The `domain_clones...` test calls `from_id(peer.cache(), fn[first])` after the file was rewritten and deleted. It still gets `fn first() {}`, so it used the cached file. `file_constructors...` and `selected_contents_outlive_handles_and_later_file_edits` check that the selected id and text are right (`second`, `fn check_token() {...}`). They also check that the selected fingerprint equals the one from `root.select`.

3. Both constructors infer the language from the filename under `requirements.sdk.outlines.defaults`. `file_constructors...` uses `AUTH.RS`, so it covers case-insensitive extension matching. It asserts the `rust-structural-v1` scheme and Rust selectors for both `from_path` and `from_id`. `selected_contents_outlive_handles_and_later_file_edits` uses `notes.unknown`, so it covers the plain-text fallback with one child per nonblank line (3 items, `second` selected) through both `from_path` and `from_id`. The mapping for each individual language belongs to the cited defaults requirement, which has its own tests (for example `default_language_names_match_the_retained_outline`).

4. Trait implementations. `Clone` is tested by `retained = cached.clone()` still selecting after the originals are dropped. `Debug` is tested by the `format!("{selected:?}")` assertion. `NodeContents` is tested by `format()`, `fingerprint()` and the scheme checks.

The other listed methods (`from_source`, `*_with`, `source_span*`, `language`) also have tests in `outline_content.rs`. They are not the subject of the prose obligations, and they belong to refining or related requirements. `public_exports_match_the_appendix` checks that the signatures are exported.

I found no gap.
